html:
SMTO-GWT-0027 — SMTO doesn't know whether the Gateway finished this action

GUID: c6d3d88f-d65f-4e14-87d0-5fd273227000
Slug: gateway-outcome-unknown
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • SMTO sent the action to the Gateway but never got a clear answer back. The action may already have run and changed something, so SMTO did not try it again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Technical details in this panel and note which command or file the action was about. You need to know exactly what to look for on the Gateway computer.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for this Gateway. A lost answer often means the connection dropped, and SMTO needs it working to look at the Gateway computer for you.
  3. Check that thing directly, for example open the file or folder, or ask SMTO in a new message to only look and report whether the change is there. The action may have finished even though the answer got lost on the way back.
  4. Only if the change is not there, ask SMTO to do the action again. Repeating an action that already ran could apply it twice, for example adding the same text again.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed the change is in place, or you repeated it once and SMTO reports it finished.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't repeat the action until someone has confirmed it did not already run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway operation was sent but no valid completion receipt was obtained (lost response, interrupted stream, or an invalid or contradictory receipt), so the operation may have taken effect and its outcome is unconfirmed.

What this means

  • The controller could not obtain a usable completion receipt for the Gateway operation. Restoring a connection proves only that communication works again; it does not establish whether the earlier command or file change ran. Reconcile the exact operation and target state before any repeat.

Why this can happen

  • The Gateway completion receipt was lost, incomplete or invalid after possible dispatch.

How to diagnose it

  • After reconnecting to the verified Gateway, inspect the existing operation or job receipt and current target state. A healthy Gateway alone is not evidence that the earlier operation failed or succeeded.

How to fix it

  • Treat the operation as possibly applied: inspect the actual target state on the Gateway (file contents, process or job state, remote resource) for the exact operation and target in Technical details before any repeat. Restoring connectivity (Check connection) only proves communication; it does not establish whether the earlier command or file change ran, so resubmit only if the effect is confirmed absent.
  • Inspect and reconcile the authoritative remote resource or job state before repeating a mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation has a trustworthy correlated terminal receipt or its effects are reconciled against current target state. Unresolved outcomes remain fenced.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • A missing or invalid Gateway completion response cannot establish an operation’s external outcome.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
